assertionReduction.reason: Each consolidated contract keeps one validation-result assertion and one independent complete-output assertion for several previously separate validation/field pairs. Redundant setup and scalar expectations are removed. Negative object/array inputs are cloned independently of their expected fixtures. This changes failure localization and test isolation; fewer expects alone do not establish equal detection.

preservedBoundaries: All compile-cache, compileStrict, circular/deep reference, prototype-pollution, Object.hasOwn and branching $ref DoS tests remain unchanged apart from Prettier line wrapping.
Boolean case variants and actual boolean; malformed/non-JSON strings; invalid/decimal numeric strings; object/array/null/NaN/Infinity string targets retain independent runtime rows.

Initially valid inputs remain in the boolean scalar, JSON version, round-trip, cache and strict-validation groups. Guard values consolidated with invalid siblings are now observed through all coercion passes.
Permanently failing sibling/missing-required cases retain failure-path mutation checks separately from successful coercion contracts.
All prefixItems/default-draft tuple, nested uniform-array, unresolved reference, two/three-hop reference, additionalProperties and no-properties object boundaries remain represented.
risks: A failure in the validation-result assertion stops the consolidated output assertion; complete-output diffs identify multiple fields but old individual case names disappear.
Combining independent schemas into one larger schema changes compilation/cache identity and execution ordering; cache-specific contracts remain independent.
Previously valid standalone guard values now also appear in invalid-sibling contracts. Full module mutation and historical fault replay remain required before retention.

Complete utils/schemaValidator.ts mutation including static mutants, with frozen input set
Applicable historical schema faults with healthy baseline and candidate runs
